sights.n: Miyako Jinja — Japan's southernmost shrine, Hirara (宮古神社)
sights.w: Founded in 1590 (Tenshō 18), Miyako Jinja is the southernmost Shinto shrine in Japan. It enshrines the three Kumano deities alongside three deified Miyako chieftains (tuyumya), including Nakasone Tuyumya; its annual festival falls on 26 October.
sights.k: Japan's southernmost Shinto shrine, in central Hirara

sights.n: Imgya Marine Garden, Gusukube (イムギャーマリンガーデン)
sights.w: A city-run seaside park built around a natural, wave-sheltered inlet (Imgya / Ingya coast) on Miyako's south shore, set up to promote marine recreation and tourism; the calm water suits snorkelling and a walking trail climbs to a lookout over the cove.
sights.k: Calm natural inlet for snorkelling on Miyako's south coast

sights.w: The cape at Miyako's north-western tip, facing the East China Sea, with a lookout over Ikema Ōhashi and Ikema Island. Its wind turbines were felled by typhoons in 2002–03 and three were rebuilt in 2008.
sights.k: Wind-turbine cape with a panorama of Ikema Ōhashi
